# k0rdent_instance_group (Data Source)

One instance group, read rather than managed.

Use it to reference a group another configuration owns. It carries the per-pool ready counts and the reservation phase, which is how far provisioning has actually got: the `k0rdent_instance_group` resource cannot carry those without reporting drift every time hardware moves underneath it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read a group of bare hosts another configuration owns.

data "k0rdent_instance_group" "inference" {
  id = "inference-fleet"
}

# Pools with fewer ready hosts than asked for. Normal for a while after a
# create or a scale.
output "pools_short_of_hosts" {
  value = [
    for name, p in data.k0rdent_instance_group.inference.node_pools : name
    if p.ready_count != null && p.ready_count < p.desired_count
  ]
}

# Quote this when asking support about a failed group.
output "execution_id" {
  value = data.k0rdent_instance_group.inference.execution_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Instance group name. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Read-Only

- `cluster_type` (String) The bound ClusterType version, whose pools describe the hardware this group is provisioned from.
- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, for display only.
- `execution_id` (String) The workflow execution behind an operation in progress, or behind a recent failure. This is the handle to quote when asking the platform team what happened. Null on a settled group that has nothing outstanding.
- `node_pools` (Attributes Map) Per-pool status as the platform reports it, keyed by the ClusterType pool name. `ready_count + not_ready_count` is the hosts a pool actually holds, so `desired_count` minus that is a shortfall the platform could not fill. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pools))
- `progress_updated_at` (String) When the per-pool progress in `node_pools` last moved, in RFC 3339. A value that stops advancing while the group is in flight is a stalled reservation. Null until the platform has recorded any progress.
- `security_groups` (List of String) Security groups applied to the group's instances. Order is significant: it is the order the fabric applies them in.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this instance group.
- `ssh_access` (Attributes Set) Linux users written onto every host in the group when it was created, each with the public keys allowed to log in as that user. Null when the group was created without any, or when the platform does not return them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ssh_access))
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state. `active` is settled.
- `state_message` (String) The platform's own explanation of the current state.
- `state_reason` (String) Machine-readable cause of the last recorded failure, such as `INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY`. Stable enough to branch on. Also set on a group that settled back to `active` after a failed scale. Null when no failure is recorded.

<a id="nestedatt--node_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_pools`

Read-Only:

- `desired_count` (Number) Hosts asked for. Only a create or a scale changes it, so it stays at the request when the platform found fewer hosts.
- `machine_type` (String) The machine type behind the pool. **Known gap.** A name only. A tenant can't read what hardware or image it is. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change.
- `not_ready_count` (Number) Hosts attached but not usable yet, or on their way out. Null whenever `ready_count` is.
- `ready_count` (Number) Hosts provisioned and usable now. Null when the platform could not read the pool's reservation, never 0 in its place.
- `reservation_phase` (String) How far the hardware reservation behind this pool has got, while the group is in flight.


<a id="nestedatt--ssh_access"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ssh_access`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name for this entry.
- `ssh_public_keys` (List of String) Public keys, each one `authorized_keys` line, allowed to log in as this user. From 1 to 32. The platform accepts `ssh-ed25519`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521`, `ssh-rsa` of at least 2048 bits, and the `sk-` security-key variants. Kept in the order written. A key must not start or end with whitespace, since the platform trims it: read one from a file with `trimspace(file(...))`, because `file()` keeps the trailing newline.
- `sudo` (String) A sudo fragment granting this user privileges, such as `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL`.
- `username` (String) Linux username to provision on every host. Must match `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`.
